name: Edaravone
aliases: 3-methyl-1-phenyl-5-pyrazolone, 1-phenyl-3-methyl-5-oxo-2-pyrazoline, 3-methyl-1-phenyl-2-pyrazolin-5-one, 3-methyl-1-phenylpyrazol-5-one, C.I. developer 1, developer Z, methylphenylpyrazolone, norphenazone
summary: Edaravone, sold under the brand name Radicava among others, is a medication used to treat stroke and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). It is given by intravenous infusion and by mouth.

pharmacology.text: The mechanism by which edaravone might be effective is unknown. The medication is known to be an antioxidant, and oxidative stress has been hypothesized to be part of the process of neurodegeneration. The half-life of edaravone is 4.5 to 6 hours and the half-lives of its metabolites are 2 to 3 hours. It is metabolized to a sulfate conjugate and a glucuronide conjugate, neither of which are active.

uses.text: Edaravone is used to help people recover from stroke in Japan, and is used to treat ALS in the US and Japan.

sideEffects.text: The most common side effects include bruising (contusions), problems walking (gait disturbances), and headaches.
